title: Modern Masters
description: The turn into modernism — symbolism and expression at the dawn of the new century.

items.title: The Scream
items.medium: Lithograph in black ink on cream card
items.description_narrative: In this lithograph, a central figure clutches their head, emitting a silent scream against a swirling, abstracted landscape. The stark black ink on cream card emphasizes the anguished form and the dramatic, unsettling lines.
items.tags: anxiety, despair, expressionism, figure, lithograph, landscape, symbolism

items.title: Madonna
items.medium: Handcolored lithograph in black on mottled gray-blue wove paper (discolored to gray-green), laid down on white wove paper
items.description_narrative: This handcolored lithograph by Edvard Munch presents a striking Madonna figure, rendered with bold lines and a somber palette. Created in 1895-1896, it is a significant example of the artist's printmaking endeavors.
items.tags: madonna, female figure, symbolism, expressionism, printmaking, lithograph, norwegian art

items.title: The Sick Child
items.medium: Drypoint in black on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: This drypoint by Edvard Munch depicts a somber scene of a sick child, reflecting themes of illness and vulnerability. Created in 1894, it showcases Munch's mastery of printmaking to convey profound emotional states.
items.tags: illness, child, drypoint, symbolism, expressionism, anxiety, psychological, modern art

items.title: Male Nude with Left Foot on a Pedestal
items.medium: Graphite and white heightening on brown wove paper
items.description_narrative: This early drawing by Gustav Klimt depicts a male nude, rendered with graphite and white heightening on brown wove paper. It serves as a foundational academic study, demonstrating the artist's skill in anatomical representation.
items.tags: male nude, figure study, academic drawing, graphite, early work, Austrian art

items.title: Male Nude
items.medium: Various graphite pencils, with erasing and stumping, on cream laid paper
items.description_narrative: Gustav Klimt's 'Male Nude', created in 1880, demonstrates the artist's early academic drawing proficiency. This figure study utilizes various graphite pencils, alongside erasing and stumping techniques, on cream laid paper.
items.tags: male nude, figure study, academic drawing, graphite, early work, human form, drawing

items.title: Seated Woman from the Front with Hat, Face Hooded
items.medium: Graphite, with colored pencil, on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Gustav Klimt's 1910 drawing captures a seated woman, her face obscured by a hood and hat, rendered with precise lines. This work in graphite and colored pencil on ivory wove paper exemplifies the artist's draftsmanship and intimate approach to figure studies.
items.tags: drawing, figure study, woman, portraiture, art nouveau, modernism, austrian art

items.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Gustave Caillebotte's 'Paris Street; Rainy Day' captures a striking urban scene in 1877 Paris, depicting well-dressed figures strolling under umbrellas on a wet street. The composition offers a unique perspective of modern city life, characterized by its precise realism and distinctive viewpoints.
items.tags: urban life, street scene, rainy day, 19th century, realism, city, umbrellas, french art

items.title: Hercules and the Lernaean Hydra
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Gustave Moreau's 'Hercules and the Lernaean Hydra' dramatically depicts the heroic figure surveying the slain multi-headed monster amid a landscape strewn with its victims. This powerful work exemplifies Moreau's Symbolist approach, rich with intricate details and a somber, mythical atmosphere.
items.tags: mythology, symbolism, hercules, hydra, french, heroic, dramatic, oil painting

items.title: Calf's Head and Ox Tongue
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: This painting presents a starkly realistic still life featuring a butchered calf's head and an ox tongue, rendered with unflinching detail. Gustave Caillebotte's meticulous brushwork captures the textures and forms of the meat, reflecting his mastery of realistic depiction.
items.tags: still life, realism, meat, food, detailed, oil painting, 19th century

items.title: Alpine Scene
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Gustave Doré's 'Alpine Scene' from 1865 captures the majestic beauty of mountainous landscapes through oil on canvas. This painting exemplifies his ability to render dramatic natural environments with intricate detail and atmospheric depth.
items.tags: landscape, alpine, mountains, oil painting, 19th century, romanticism, french, sublime

items.title: Mère Grégoire
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's 'Mère Grégoire' is an oil on canvas portrait depicting an older woman. This work exemplifies Courbet's commitment to portraying everyday people with directness and realism.
items.tags: portrait, woman, realism, french realism, direct, naturalistic, oil painting

items.title: The Rock of Hautepierre
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's 'The Rock of Hautepierre' depicts a rugged natural landscape with a prominent rock formation. This oil on canvas exemplifies Courbet's commitment to Realism, capturing the unadorned beauty of the natural world.
items.tags: landscape, realism, nature, oil painting, rock formation, french art

items.title: An Alpine Scene
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's "An Alpine Scene" captures a dramatic mountain landscape, rendered with the artist's characteristic impasto technique. This oil on canvas work from 1874 exemplifies his dedication to depicting natural subjects with unflinching realism.
items.tags: landscape, Realism, oil painting, French art, mountain, nature, alpine, Courbet

items.title: The Valley of Les Puits-Noir
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's 'The Valley of Les Puits-Noir' depicts a rugged, unidealized landscape from his native Jura region in eastern France. Executed in oil on canvas, this work exemplifies his Realist approach, capturing nature with a somber palette and textured brushwork.
items.tags: landscape, realism, french art, 19th century, nature, valley, oil painting

items.title: Rêverie (Portrait of Gabrielle Borreau)
items.medium: Oil on paper, mounted on canvas
items.description_narrative: This intimate portrait by Gustave Courbet depicts Gabrielle Borreau in a contemplative pose. Painted in 1862, the work captures a moment of quiet introspection.
items.tags: portrait, realism, 19th century, contemplative, figure study, oil painting, french art

items.title: Cliffs on the Sea Coast: Small Beach, Sunrise (Falaise au bord de la mer, vu Petite Plage, soleil levant)
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet captures the rugged beauty of a coastal scene in 'Cliffs on the Sea Coast: Small Beach, Sunrise.' This oil on canvas painting from 1865 depicts a dramatic interplay of light and shadow on the cliffs as the sun rises over the sea.
items.tags: seascape, landscape, realism, nature, cliffs, sunrise, oil painting

items.title: Study for Paris Street; Rainy Day
items.medium: Graphite, with touches of erasing and touches of charcoal, on tan, moderately thick, moderately textured handmade laid paper
items.description_narrative: This detailed graphite and charcoal study by Gustave Caillebotte explores the composition and figures for his seminal work, "Paris Street; Rainy Day." Executed in 1877, it captures the structured urban planning and bourgeois life characteristic of Impressionist Paris.
items.tags: paris, street scene, urban life, impressionism, drawing, preparatory study, figure study, 19th century

items.title: Sketchbook
items.medium: Sketchbook containing 40 drawings: 30 in graphite, 7 in watercolor over graphite, and 3 in graphite and brush and gray wash, on 40 sheets of cream wove paper bound in brown cloth
items.description_narrative: This sketchbook by Gustave Caillebotte contains 40 drawings, showcasing his prolific artistic practice. The collection features graphite, watercolor, and brush and gray wash works across its cream wove paper sheets.
items.tags: sketchbook, drawings, graphite, watercolor, studies, 19th century, preliminary works

items.title: The Brook of Les Puits-Noir
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet captures the quiet solitude of a brook winding through a densely wooded landscape in Les Puits-Noir. This painting exemplifies his commitment to depicting unidealized nature with a robust, earthy palette.
items.tags: landscape, nature, brook, forest, realism, 19th-century art, tranquil

items.title: Self-Portrait with a Hat
items.medium: Graphite on off-white, medium-weight, moderately textured laid paper
items.description_narrative: This self-portrait by Gustave Caillebotte captures the artist in graphite, presenting a direct gaze. Executed on textured laid paper, it showcases his skill in drawing.
items.tags: self-portrait, male, drawing, graphite, french, 19th century, impressionism

items.title: Inspiration
items.medium: Watercolor and gouache, with pen and blue ink, over traces of graphite, on ivory wove paper, wrapped and adhered on verso to wood pulp board
items.description_narrative: "Inspiration" by Gustave Moreau is a delicate work rendered in watercolor and gouache with pen and blue ink. This composition reflects the artist's characteristic exploration of mythical and allegorical themes, often associated with the Symbolist movement.
items.tags: Gustave Moreau, watercolor, gouache, Symbolism, allegory, French art, 19th century

items.title: The Girl by the Window
items.medium: Oil on canvas
items.description_narrative: Edvard Munch's The Girl by the Window captures a moment of introspection and quiet solitude. This work exemplifies the artist's exploration of psychological states through the depiction of figures in evocative settings.
items.tags: expressionism, symbolism, psychological, solitude, figure painting, norwegian art, fin de siècle

items.title: Two Women on the Shore
items.medium: Woodcut printed from one block (sawn into three sections) in dark blue, green, black and red-brown ink with additions in green crayon on cream Japanese paper
items.description_narrative: Edvard Munch's 1898 woodcut, "Two Women on the Shore," depicts two figures by the water's edge. This work showcases Munch's innovative printmaking technique, utilizing a single block sawn into multiple sections to achieve distinct color areas.
items.tags: two women, shore, woodcut, expressionism, printmaking, melancholic, landscape

items.title: Consolation
items.medium: Drypoint and open bite in black on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: Edvard Munch's "Consolation" exemplifies his mastery of printmaking through the intricate techniques of drypoint and open bite. Created in 1894, this work likely explores profound human emotions, a central theme in the Norwegian artist's oeuvre.
items.tags: symbolism, expressionism, printmaking, drypoint, emotional, psychological, melancholy, late 19th century

items.title: The Sick Child I
items.medium: Transfer lithograph printed from two stones in pale blue and black ink on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This transfer lithograph, 'The Sick Child I,' depicts a poignant scene centered on a young, ailing figure. Created by Edvard Munch, it explores themes of illness, mortality, and human vulnerability, reflecting his personal experiences and characteristic emotional depth.
items.tags: symbolism, expressionism, illness, child, melancholy, lithograph, portrait, printmaking

items.title: The Dead Mother and Her Child
items.medium: Etching with open bite and drypoint in black ink on heavyweight cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: Edvard Munch's 1901 etching, 'The Dead Mother and Her Child', masterfully employs open bite and drypoint techniques to create a stark, emotional scene. This powerful work portrays profound grief and the chilling presence of death through its somber figures and dark tones.
items.tags: death, grief, mother, child, etching, printmaking, expressionism, symbolism

items.title: Boys Bathing
items.medium: Color burnished aquatint, inked à la poupée, on buff laid paper
items.description_narrative: This vibrant color aquatint by Edvard Munch depicts a group of boys engaged in bathing, capturing a moment of youthful activity. The artist's innovative use of burnished aquatint and à la poupée inking creates rich tones and a distinctive texture, characteristic of his graphic work.
items.tags: boys, bathing, figures, printmaking, aquatint, color print, Norwegian, expressionist

items.title: Young Woman on the Beach
items.medium: Burnished aquatint and drypoint in purple, blue, gray and yellow, inked à la poupée, on cream laid Arches paper
items.description_narrative: This print by Edvard Munch depicts a solitary young woman on a beach, rendered with burnished aquatint and drypoint. The artist utilized a sophisticated à la poupée inking technique, applying purple, blue, gray, and yellow inks to create a nuanced composition on cream laid Arches paper.
items.tags: printmaking, aquatint, drypoint, figure, beach, symbolism, expressionism, melancholic

items.title: Man Bathing
items.medium: Color woodcut from two blocks on grayish ivory card
items.description_narrative: This striking color woodcut depicts a lone male figure in the act of bathing. Edvard Munch utilized two blocks to create this powerful image, showcasing the distinctive textures and bold forms inherent in the woodcut technique.
items.tags: man, nude, bathing, woodcut, printmaking, expressionism, figural

items.title: The Brooch. Eva Mudocci
items.medium: Lithograph on thin Japanese paper
items.description_narrative: This striking lithograph portrays the Danish violinist Eva Mudocci, a subject frequently depicted by Edvard Munch. Mudocci gazes directly at the viewer, her face framed by dark hair and adorned with a prominent brooch.
items.tags: portrait, lithograph, Eva Mudocci, woman, musician, printmaking, introspective, early 20th century
